thesis: Allah grounds the command about parents in the mother's physical wahn — a fact prior to and unnegotiated by the quality of the relationship — and 31:15 then commands the child to hold refusal (in shirk only) and companionship simultaneously.

flags.quote: The sound narration on this exact point is the report of Jāhima, recorded by al-Nasāʾī in his *Sunan*. ... And the Prophet ﷺ told him: *ilzamhā* — **stay close to her** — *fa-thamma l-janna* — **for Paradise is there.**
flags.issue: NEW ERROR INTRODUCED BY THE REPAIR. The wording is not al-Nasa'i's. Al-Nasa'i (Sunan, K. al-Jihad, #3104, Mu'awiya b. Jahima al-Sulami) reads: فالزمها فإن الجنة تحت رجليها — 'cling to her, for Paradise is beneath her feet' (a variant in Sahih al-Targhib: فإن الجنة عند رجلها). The wording quoted in the file — الزم رجلها فثم الجنة — is SUNAN IBN MAJAH's (#2781). So the repair swapped one collection's wording under another collection's name. This is doubly damaging because the repair's whole rhetorical move is 'the popular wording is weak, here is the sound narration correctly attributed' — and al-Nasa'i's actual sound wording is the very 'beneath her feet' phrasing the paragraph just declined to use. The paragraph that follows ('That is not a compliment paid to mothers. It is a redirection... the road does not run past her. It runs where she is.') is built on the misquoted half. Verified against two independent sources (islamweb fatwa 58735; dorar.net Mawsu'a Hadithiyya / hadithprophet.com for Nasa'i 3104); sunnah.com returned HTTP 403. FIX: either attribute فثم الجنة to Ibn Majah, or quote al-Nasa'i's actual wording and rebuild the 'redirection vs. compliment' point on it.

flags.quote: ### 1. *Waṣṣaynā* and *Wahnan ʿalā Wahn* — The Weighted Testament and the Weakness That Builds
flags.issue: RESIDUAL ARTIFACT of the removed false-morphology claim. The repair correctly deleted the 'Form II is one level more intense than Form IV / weight of a last will and testament' argument and added the explicit disclaimer 'it is not the deathbed-will form, and it would be dishonest to borrow that colour for it' and 'Not one of them reaches for a will or a bequest.' But the testament framing survives in FIVE places and now directly contradicts the file's own new statement: the section heading above; line 93 'And what is the content of this testament?'; line 119 'the Creator of both bodies has made a binding testament that you will not forget this'; line 187 'The full weight of the testament still stands'; line 241 'The testament has a deadline.' FIX: rename the heading and replace the four body occurrences with 'command'/'injunction' (the repairer already did exactly this at lines 285 and 297).

flags.quote: He went to the Prophet ﷺ — devastated, torn apart, loving her more than he could bear — and this ayah was revealed about that exact moment.
flags.issue: PRE-EXISTING, not repair-introduced. None of the four fetched editions has Sa'd going to the Prophet ﷺ. Ibn Kathir (via at-Tabarani) and al-Tabari's four chains (Simak b. Harb / Mus'ab b. Sa'd) report only the exchange between Sa'd and his mother and her family force-feeding her. Narrative embellishment beyond the sources.

notes: Defects (i) and (ii) VERIFY CLEANLY; defect (iii) introduced a new misattribution. Corpus check on root وصي confirms the repair's morphology exactly: TESTAMENT register is Form IV — 4:11 yūṣī x2, 4:12 tūṣū/yūṣā/yūṣī (all VF:4), 19:31 awṣā (VF:4), 2:182 mūṣin (VF:4), noun waṣiyya at 2:180, 2:240, 4:11, 4:12, 5:106 — while Form II waṣṣā is the routine injunction form at 2:132, 4:131, 6:144, 6:151, 6:152, 6:153, 29:8, 31:14, 42:13 (x2), 46:15 (the file lists all of these). Fixed-formula claim VERIFIED: after normalization, 29:8, 46:15 and 31:14 all open with ووصينا الانسن بولديه, so 31:14 is a standing formula, not a marked escalation. All four editions' glosses quoted in the repair are EXACT: al-Tabari وأمرنا الإنسان ببرّ والديه; al-Muyassar وأَمَرْنا الإنسان ببرِّ والديه والإحسان إليهما; al-Jalalayn أمَرْناهُ أنْ يَبَرّهُما; Ibn Kathir 'enjoined'. Breadth claim 'Not one of them reaches for a will or a bequest' names all four individually and holds. Defect (ii) VERIFIED: 46:15 reads ثلثون شهرا, and Ibn Kathir on 31:14 does derive the six-month minimum pregnancy from it ('Ibn 'Abbas and other Imams understood that the shortest possible period of pregnancy was six months'); the word 'minimum' is gone from both places and the new wording ('roughly thirty-three months in the ordinary case'; 'thirty at the classical minimum') is accurate. Also verified exact: al-Tabari's ضعفا على ضعف، وشدّة على شدّة; the Zuhayr rope verse; al-Muyassar's inserted ثم in اشكر لله، ثم اشكر لوالديك; al-Muyassar's لا طاعة لمخلوق في معصية الخالق. Two fixes needed: the al-Nasa'i wording, and the five residual 'testament' occurrences.

thesis: Al-Mulk 1-5 descends from a verb used of no one but Allah, through death-as-created and the purpose of the test, to a dare to find one flaw in the heavens that sends the human gaze back humbled and exhausted.
notes: ALL FOUR REPAIRS VERIFY EXACTLY. (i) The i'jaz 'ilmi paragraph ('what fourteen centuries of astronomy have confirmed... the laws of physics at the edge of the observable universe...') is GONE and replaced with an explicit refusal ('The tempting move is to reach for modern astronomy and say that science has now confirmed the dare. The commentators do not read the verse that way at all'). Ibn Kathir's tafawut gloss is quoted verbatim ('in a flawless manner... having no disunion, conflict, inconsistency, deficiency, flaw or defect') and the futur chain is exactly as fetched: Ibn 'Abbas, Mujahid, Ad-Dahhak, Ath-Thawri = cracks; As-Suddi = tears; Qatadah = 'do you see any defects O Son of Adam'. All construction-language, no physical-law claim — the file says so and it is right. Qatadah's warning at 67:5 is REAL and quoted correctly: 'whoever seeks to interpret any other meanings for them other than these, then verily he has spoken with his own opinion, he has lost his portion and burdened himself with that which he has no knowledge of' (Ibn Kathir, end of the 1-5 block; recorded by Ibn Jarir and Ibn Abi Hatim), and the three stated purposes (adornment / missiles / navigation) are accurate. One small slippage worth knowing: Qatadah's warning is about interpreting THE STARS beyond three purposes; the file's gloss widens it to 'do not make the sky say things it was not sent to say.' The file does state the stars framing correctly first, so this is paraphrase drift, not misattribution. (ii) MORPHOLOGY FIXED CORRECTLY: ta'allama (Form V) is gone; the replacement example yatasā'alūn at 37:27 is confirmed VF:6 in the corpus (37:27:5:1 IMPF|VF:6|ROOT:سأل), and tabāraka itself is VF:6 (9 occurrences: 7:54, 23:14, 25:1, 25:10, 25:61, 40:64, 43:85, 55:78, 67:1 — every one of them 3MS of Allah, so the 'exclusively for Allah in the Quran' claim also verifies). tashāraka was correctly left intact as a language-level Form VI example. (iii) BAD ATTRIBUTION FIXED: the barakah derivation is now credited to al-Muyassar and his Arabic is quoted verbatim — تكاثر خير الله وبرُّه على جميع خلقه. The parenthetical that Ibn Kathir 'does not go that route... opens by saying Allah is glorifying His own Noble Self and announcing that the dominion is in His Hand' matches Ibn Kathir exactly. The adjacent al-Tabari attribution is intact and now MORE accurate than before: al-Tabari's literal words are تعاظم وتعالى and the file gives 'ta'azama wa ta'ala'. (iv) REATTRIBUTION CORRECT: Ibn Kathir reads ahsan as 'best in deeds. This is as Muhammad bin 'Ajlan said. It should be noted that Allah did not say which of you does the most deeds' — the file now states this precisely, and it demotes the al-Fudayl ibn 'Iyad dictum with an explicit hedge ('not in Ibn Kathir's comment here, so take it as a well-known dictum rather than as this verse's classical gloss') rather than substituting an unverifiable citation. Three PRE-EXISTING minor items for the human, none repair-introduced and none thesis-bearing: (a) al-Zajjaj and al-Razi are cited but sit outside the four fetched editions, so unverifiable here — al-Zajjaj's ta'ala is at least corroborated in substance by al-Tabari's تعاظم وتعالى; (b) 'a single word that exists nowhere else in Arabic in quite this form' is loose — the tafā'ala pattern is ordinary Arabic; what is actually true (and correctly stated two paragraphs later) is that the Qur'an uses it only of Allah; (c) the Ibn 'Abbas tent-over-a-grave narration is given without a named collection (it is at-Tirmidhi), which is the same class of issue the Luqman repair was about — worth naming the collection for consistency.

thesis: 17:26-30 treats wealth as a moral and theological object — rights owed before generosity, waste as shaytanic ingratitude, gentleness owed even when one cannot give, and rizq relocated to Allah's expanding and constricting.

flags.quote: The instinct is to hear *tabdhir* as a quantity word — spending too much, scattering too widely. The classical definition is not about quantity at all. It is about **where the money goes.**
flags.issue: NEW OVERCLAIM INTRODUCED BY THE REPAIR — an over-correction in the opposite direction. The qualitative reports the repair added are all real and quoted accurately, but 'not about quantity at all' is false against the sources, and it fails the breadth-of-attribution rule in the textbook way: the paragraph names al-Tabari, Ibn Kathir and al-Jalalayn, and the UNNAMED fourth edition is the one that carries the quantity sense. (1) al-Muyassar 17:26: ولا تنفق مالك في غير طاعة الله، أو على وجه الإسراف والتبذير — 'or by way of israf and tabdhir', an explicit extravagance clause. (2) al-Tabari's OWN lexical note in the same passage: وأصل التبذير: التفريق في السّرَف — 'the root sense of tabdhir is dispersal in extravagance' — and he illustrates it with a poetry shahid on al-mubadhdhar. (3) Ibn Kathir's own framing is squarely quantitative: 'When Allah commands spending, He forbids extravagance. Spending should be moderate,' citing 25:67 وَالَّذِينَ إِذَا أَنفَقُوا لَمْ يُسْرِفُوا وَلَمْ يَقْتُرُوا, then 'to discourage extravagance'; and he glosses ikhwan al-shayatin as 'brothers in extravagance, foolishness.' (4) Even one of the Ibn Mas'ud chains reads التبذير في غير الحقّ، وهو الإسراف. FIX: 'the DOMINANT classical definition is qualitative' rather than 'not about quantity at all', plus one clause naming al-Muyassar and al-Tabari's asl as keeping the extravagance sense — which is a stronger paragraph anyway, since Mujahid's criterion is a real minority-sharpening against that background, not a consensus.

notes: Defect (ii) — the ikhtilaf section and the tadabbur-vs-fatwa line — is EXEMPLARY and fully verified line by line against al-Tabari 17:26; defect (i) fixed the quantitative gap but introduced the overclaim above. IKHTILAF VERIFIED EXACT: al-Tabari's 17:26 commentary does open with اختلف أهل التأويل في المعنيّ بقوله ﴿وآتِ ذَا القُرْبى﴾; the first group (one's own kin, father's and mother's side) is carried by al-Hasan (the man asking whether he may give his zakah to relatives, answered إن لهم في ذلك لحقا سوى الزكاة then reciting the ayah — verbatim as the file has it), 'Ikrimah, and Ibn 'Abbas (هو أن تصل ذا القرابة والمسكين وتُحسن إلى ابن السبيل — the file's rendering is exact); the second group (kin of the Messenger ﷺ) rests on the report from 'Ali b. al-Husayn to a man from Sham, including the 'have you read this in Bani Isra'il' detail; and al-Tabari rules for the first with the reason the file gives (the verse follows the command about parents) and marks it as his own view — وأولى التأويلين عندي بالصواب, quoted correctly. Second ikhtilaf VERIFIED: وقد قيل: إنما عنى بالأمر بإتيان ابن السبيل حقه أن يضاف ثلاثة أيام, with al-Tabari preferring the general reading for the stated reason (Allah did not single out one form of the right, not in His Book nor on the tongue of His Messenger) and the general reading's content (ضيافة أو حمولة أو مَعُونة على سفره = hospitality, transport, help with the journey). The section REPORTS WITHOUT ADJUDICATING and issues no ruling; the fatwa line is present and adequate for an ahkam passage, and it names the right live fiqh question (hajr — guardianship over a squanderer's property). TABDHIR CITATIONS ALL VERIFIED VERBATIM: Ibn Mas'ud إنفاق المال في غير حقه (al-Tabari carries 7-8 Ibn Mas'ud entries; exactly 6 of them with this same wording, so 'six separate chains, in the same words each time' is defensible but tight — the human may prefer 'repeatedly'); Ibn 'Abbas المبذّر: المنفق في غير حقه twice in those words (a third Ibn 'Abbas report exists with different wording); Qatadah التبذير: النفقة في معصية الله; Ibn Zayd لا تعطِ في معاصي الله; al-Jalalayn بالإنفاق في غير طاعة الله; and MUJAHID IS EXACT AND CORRECTLY REPRESENTED — al-Tabari: لو أنفق إنسان ماله كله في الحقّ ما كان تبذيرا، ولو انفق مدّا في باطل كان تبذيرا, and Ibn Kathir carries it in English identically, so the file's 'preserved by both al-Tabari and Ibn Kathir' holds and the direction of the criterion (all your wealth on what is due is NOT tabdhir; one mudd on what is false IS) is stated correctly, not inverted. The file's own framing no longer points a reader to the opposite conclusion. Also spot-verified: the 'image of sitting returns, as in verse 22' claim — 17:22 reads فَتَقْعُدَ مَذْمُومًا مَّخْذُولًا, so the فتقعد echo is real. One fix needed: the 'not about quantity at all' sentence.
